newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end weak on rolling, supply fears.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end weak on rolling, supply fears.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed lower with December pacing the loss on fund rolling and pressure from concern over increased fed cattle supplies. Feeders showed added weakness from higher corn futures, traders said.
Live cattle futures closed 0.500 to 0.150 cent lower paced by December at 66.575 cents. February ended 0.200 lower at 63.825 cents.
The market is looking for cash cattle prices to trend lower by late November or early December as more fed cattle become available for market, traders said.

"There remains a fairly consistent attitude amoungst apparently the majority of people that we are going to see the bulge in (fed cattle) numbers occur by the time we get to December," said Tom Tippens, CEO Professional Cattle Consultants Inc.

Packers were expected to have adequate contract and formula cattle numbers lined up for December to meet much of their slaughter needs. Cash cattle were seen easing to the mid $60 per cwt area, traders said.
But Tippens was not as negative to the market and only looked for live prices to slip back to the high $60's.

Tippens noted there was enough time to make marketings more current and cut slaughter weights to chip away at the expected big increase in fed supplies. Feedlots have done such a good job of marketing cattle the last six weeks there is some December cattle already heading to market.
"Once we get to December we are going to find that that bulge in numbers isn't nearly as big as we once thought," he added.
Rolling forward of fund positions added to losses in December. Refco notably bought February and sold December, pit sources added.
In live cattle options, December volatility was steady to firm and February strong. There was active spreading of long December 68 calls/short 64 puts, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle remained under pressure from an overbought condition and higher corn futures, traders said.
"Unlike the fats, feeders have been carrying a pretty big premium to the feeder index," Tippens added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.08 to $63.30 per cwt. January feeders closed off 0.675 at 66.950 cents and other months were down 0.600 to 0.350 cent.
